I'm going to Basic Training as an Airborne Infantryman recruit and I know down the line that I'll have a lot of down time on my hands so I was wondering if there was any really good immersive, action, fantasy, etc. kinds of books that you would recommend!

Oh ... you want action and fantasy ...

Can't help you there, but if you are bucking for OCS, you may want to start looking into Sawyer's Seven Military Classics of Ancient China and maybe a little of Liddell-Hart's Strategy.

Charles Royer's The Destructive War is a good read for American Civil War historians and offers some analyses of how General Sherman came to adopt his war strategy from 1862 to 1865. Also some mention of Sherman's time in the Indian Wars (about 2 paragraphs) and his reasons for conducting his command that way.
Starship Troopers by Robert A. Heinlein. Great military sci/fi book which is actually on the reading lists of the US Marine Corps and US Navy.
Gaunt's Ghosts series by Dan Abnett. It is set in the Warhammer 40k universe, and follows Gaunt's Imperial Guard unit throughout the Sabbat Worlds campaign.

If I don't have my daughter, I will go to the gym and work out. That usually will help me. If I do have my daughter, I will go sit with her and watch tv. Hearing her laugh will make me smile and help clear my head.

Activity. Any kind of activity, specifically something I wouldn't normally do: go see a band I've never heard of, eat somewhere new, walk through a place I've never stopped before, anything like that.

It works really well for anger or sadness (at least for me) because it pulls you out of your mental rut.

Clean something up. It doesn't matter what it is, just find something and clean it up. Recently I was having a bad day and I saw an old bike sitting next to my garage. It looked all rusty and out of shape so I pumped up the tires, sanded the frame down, got a new chain, painted it, and reassembled everything. In the end, I had a beautiful new functioning bike and I felt much better because of it. You can get the same effect from cleaning your room, decluttering your workspace, whatever it is. It has always helped me.
